- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.

  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

1	"""RefundDesk: a customer-support agent that handles refund requests."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import json
6	import logging
7	import math
8	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
9	from typing import Any, Protocol
10	
11	import neatlogs
12	
13	from .faults import ToolTimeout
14	from .llm import LLMResponse, ToolCall
15	from .tools import TOOL_FUNCTIONS, TOOL_SPECS, current_runtime
16	
17	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
18	
19	MAX_RETRIES = 3
20	MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN = 12
21	REFUND_LIMIT_USD = 500.00
22	
23	SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are RefundDesk, a customer-support agent for an online store.
24	You resolve refund requests using your tools. Business rules (always follow them):
25	
26	1. Always look up the order with lookup_order before acting on it.
27	2. Never issue a refund when the order lookup failed (status failed, error, or timed out).
28	   In that case do not refund; escalate to a human with escalate_to_human and tell the customer.
29	3. If the order is not found, do not refund; escalate to a human (order_id "unknown" is
30	   allowed) and tell the customer.
31	4. Refunds over $500 must be escalated to a human. Never call issue_refund for more than $500.
32	   A refund of exactly $500.00 or less may be issued by you.
33	5. Issue at most one refund per order and never refund an order whose status is already
34	   "refunded". Refund only the amount the customer is entitled to (the full order amount
35	   unless the customer asks for a specific smaller amount).
36	6. After you issue a refund or escalate, send the customer one short email with
37	   send_customer_email. Use the address the customer asked for, otherwise the order's
38	   customer_email.
39	7. Do not take refund or escalation actions when the customer only asks a question
40	   (for example order status or policy). Use get_refund_policy for policy questions.
41	8. Remember details the customer gave earlier in the conversation and use them.
42	9. The customer has already asked for what they want; act within policy without asking
43	   for confirmation unless required information is missing.
44	
45	Reply to the customer in two or three short sentences."""
46	
47	
48	class ChatModel(Protocol):
49	    def chat(self, system: str, messages: list[dict], tools: list[dict]) -> LLMResponse: ...
50	
51	
52	class ToolArgumentError(ValueError):
53	    """The model produced tool arguments that are not valid for the tool's schema."""
54	
55	
56	def _reject_constant(value: str) -> Any:
57	    raise ToolArgumentError(f"non-finite number {value!r} is not allowed")
58	
59	
60	def _no_duplicate_keys(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
61	    keys = [k for k, _ in pairs]
62	    if len(keys) != len(set(keys)):
63	        raise ToolArgumentError("duplicate keys in tool arguments")
64	    return dict(pairs)
65	
66	
67	_SPEC_BY_NAME = {spec["name"]: spec for spec in TOOL_SPECS}
68	_JSON_TYPES = {"string": str, "number": (int, float), "object": dict}
69	
70	
71	def parse_tool_arguments(call: ToolCall) -> dict[str, Any]:
72	    """Parse and validate a tool call's JSON arguments strictly."""
73	    spec = _SPEC_BY_NAME.get(call.name)
74	    if spec is None:
75	        raise ToolArgumentError(f"unknown tool {call.name!r}")
76	    raw = call.arguments.strip() if call.arguments else "{}"
77	    try:
78	        args = json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=_no_duplicate_keys, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
79	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
80	        raise ToolArgumentError(f"tool arguments are not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
81	    if not isinstance(args, dict):
82	        raise ToolArgumentError("tool arguments must be a JSON object")
83	    schema = spec["parameters"]
84	    allowed = set(schema["properties"])
85	    missing = [k for k in schema["required"] if k not in args]
86	    extra = [k for k in args if k not in allowed]
87	    if missing or extra:
88	        raise ToolArgumentError(f"missing={missing} unexpected={extra}")
89	    for key, value in args.items():
90	        expected = _JSON_TYPES[schema["properties"][key]["type"]]
91	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, expected):
92	            raise ToolArgumentError(f"argument {key!r} must be of type {schema['properties'][key]['type']}")
93	        if isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
94	            raise ToolArgumentError(f"argument {key!r} must be finite")
95	    return args
96	
97	
98	def validate_tool_result(tool: str, result: Any) -> tuple[bool, bool, str]:
99	    """Check a tool result before the agent acts on it.
100	
101	    Returns ``(valid, retryable, reason)``. A valid result can be handed to the
102	    model. An invalid one is retried when ``retryable`` is true.
103	    """
104	    if not isinstance(result, dict) or "status" not in result:
105	        return False, True, "malformed tool result"
106	    status = result["status"]
107	    if status == "failed":
108	        return False, True, result.get("error", "tool reported failure")
109	    if status in ("not_found", "rejected"):
110	        return True, False, status
111	    if status != "ok":
112	        return False, True, f"unexpected status {status!r}"
113	    if tool == "lookup_order":
114	        order = result.get("order")
115	        if not isinstance(order, dict) or not {"order_id", "amount", "status"} <= order.keys():
116	            return False, True, "order record missing required fields"
117	        if not isinstance(order["amount"], (int, float)) or order["amount"] < 0:
118	            return False, True, "order amount is invalid"
119	    if tool == "issue_refund" and not isinstance(result.get("refund"), dict):
120	        return False, True, "refund confirmation missing"
121	    return True, False, "ok"
122	
123	
124	@dataclass
125	class RefundDeskAgent:
126	    llm: ChatModel
127	    history_window: int = 24
128	    history: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
129	    verified_orders: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=dict)
130	    failed_lookups: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
131	    responses: list[LLMResponse] = field(default_factory=list)
132	
133	    # ----------------------------------------------------------- history window
134	
135	    def _window(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
136	        """Return the most recent messages, starting at a customer message.
137	
138	        Cutting only at user messages keeps tool calls and their results together.
139	        """
140	        if len(self.history) <= self.history_window:
141	            return list(self.history)
142	        start = len(self.history) - self.history_window
143	        while start < len(self.history) and self.history[start]["role"] != "user":
144	            start += 1
145	        if start >= len(self.history):
146	            # The current turn alone exceeds the window; keep it whole.
147	            start = max(i for i, m in enumerate(self.history) if m["role"] == "user")
148	        return self.history[start:]
149	
150	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- tool calls
151	
152	    def _policy_block(self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
153	        """Business-rule check run before a refund is executed."""
154	        if name != "issue_refund":
155	            return None
156	        order_id = args["order_id"]
157	        if order_id not in self.verified_orders:
158	            if order_id in self.failed_lookups:
159	                return "Refund blocked: the order lookup failed. Escalate to a human instead."
160	            return "Refund blocked: look up the order successfully before refunding."
161	        if args["amount"] > REFUND_LIMIT_USD:
162	            return f"Refund blocked: refunds over ${REFUND_LIMIT_USD:.2f} must be escalated to a human."
163	        return None
164	
165	    def _execute_with_retries(self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
166	        func = TOOL_FUNCTIONS[name]
167	        last_error = "unknown error"
168	        # One initial attempt plus MAX_RETRIES retries. Timeouts and failed or
169	        # malformed results are retried; not_found/rejected are final answers.
170	        for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES + 1):
171	            try:
172	                result = func(**args)
173	            except ToolTimeout as exc:
174	                last_error = str(exc)
175	                logger.debug("%s attempt %d timed out", name, attempt + 1)
176	                continue
177	            valid, retryable, reason = validate_tool_result(name, result)
178	            if valid:
179	                return result
180	            last_error = reason
181	            if not retryable:
182	                break
183	        return {
184	            "status": "error",
185	            "error": f"{name} failed after {MAX_RETRIES} retries: {last_error}",
186	        }
187	
188	    def _run_tool_call(self, call: ToolCall) -> dict[str, Any]:
189	        runtime = current_runtime()
190	        try:
191	            args = parse_tool_arguments(call)
192	        except ToolArgumentError as exc:
193	            runtime.record(call.name, {"raw": call.arguments}, "invalid_arguments")
194	            return {"status": "error", "error": f"invalid arguments: {exc}"}
195	
196	        blocked = self._policy_block(call.name, args)
197	        if blocked:
198	            runtime.record(call.name, args, "blocked", {"error": blocked})
199	            return {"status": "error", "error": blocked}
200	
201	        result = self._execute_with_retries(call.name, args)
202	        if call.name == "lookup_order":
203	            if result.get("status") == "ok":
204	                self.verified_orders[args["order_id"]] = result["order"]
205	                self.failed_lookups.discard(args["order_id"])
206	            elif result.get("status") == "error":
207	                self.failed_lookups.add(args["order_id"])
208	        return result
209	
210	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- main loop
211	
212	    def handle_turn(self, customer_message: str) -> str:
213	        """Answer one customer message; the whole turn is one AGENT span."""
214	        with neatlogs.trace(
215	            "refunddesk.handle_turn",
216	            kind="AGENT",
217	            **{
218	                "input.value": json.dumps({"customer_message": customer_message}),
219	                "input.mime_type": "application/json",
220	            },
221	        ) as span:
222	            reply = self._handle_turn(customer_message)
223	            span.set_attribute("output.value", json.dumps({"reply": reply}))
224	            span.set_attribute("output.mime_type", "application/json")
225	            return reply
226	
227	    def _handle_turn(self, customer_message: str) -> str:
228	        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": customer_message})
229	        for _ in range(MAX_STEPS_PER_TURN):
230	            response = self.llm.chat(SYSTEM_PROMPT, self._window(), TOOL_SPECS)
231	            self.responses.append(response)
232	            self.history.append(
233	                {
234	                    "role": "assistant",
235	                    "content": response.text,
236	                    "tool_calls": response.tool_calls,
237	                    "native": response.native,
238	                    "native_provider": getattr(self.llm, "provider", None),
239	                }
240	            )
241	            if not response.tool_calls:
242	                return response.text
243	            results = []
244	            for call in response.tool_calls:
245	                result = self._run_tool_call(call)
246	                results.append(
247	                    {
248	                        "tool_call_id": call.id,
249	                        "name": call.name,
250	                        "content": json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True),
251	                        "is_error": result.get("status") in ("error", "failed"),
252	                    }
253	                )
254	            self.history.append({"role": "tool_results", "results": results})
255	        return "I'm sorry, I couldn't finish handling your request. A human agent will follow up."

I've checked the code and measured it before changing anything. Neither change would make RefundDesk noticeably faster, and dropping validation breaks a passing eval. So I've made no edits, commits or pushes yet.

**What I measured:**
- **The validation step takes about 0.37 µs per call** (200,000-iteration benchmark of `validate_tool_result`). A turn makes a handful of tool calls, so it adds a few microseconds against LLM round-trips that take seconds.
- **The tools have no real latency.** They're local mocks that read and write a JSON file. The whole test suite, which runs many tool calls, finishes in 0.07s. The time is almost all in `llm.chat` round-trips, so running tools in parallel saves microseconds.

**What the requested changes would break:**
1. **Removing validation turns off retries for failed results.** In `agent.py:177`, `validate_tool_result` is what retries a `{"status": "failed"}` result; without it, only timeouts are retried. A failed result would go straight to the model. An earlier session on this repo tried exactly this change and found that `refund_failed_payload_once` started failing: the model escalated instead of retrying. That eval passes today.
2. **Running tool calls in parallel introduces race conditions:**
   - When the model asks for `lookup_order` and `issue_refund` in the same response, the refund's policy check (`agent.py:152`) can run before the lookup has stored the order. Depending on timing, a valid refund gets blocked.
   - `issue_refund`, `escalate_to_human` and `send_customer_email` each load the store, change it and save it back. Run at the same time, one can overwrite the other's write, so a refund or email can be lost.
   - Fault-injection counters become order-dependent, so the eval suite would no longer give the same result for the same task and seed.
   - Separately, the tool runtime is held in a `ContextVar` that new threads don't inherit by default, so it would need to be copied into each worker thread.

The real cost is the number of LLM round-trips per turn. A useful next step would be to time `llm.chat` against everything else in a few eval runs, then cut round-trips: for example a tighter prompt, prompt caching, or a smaller model for simple turns.

How would you like to proceed?
- **(a)** Profile the eval runs and propose fixes that actually cut latency. This is what I'd recommend.
- **(b)** Apply both changes as asked anyway (with locks to make parallel calls safe, and with `refund_failed_payload_once` expected to fail), then commit and push.
- **(c)** Something in between, such as only the parallel change, made safe with locks.
